- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike, reduce forecast by 10–15% for the next 3–5 periods to account for mean reversion.  
- If forecast peaks early and true outcome lags, adjust downward by 5–8% in subsequent periods to reflect delayed reaction.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating >0.3) and forecast is erratic, apply smoothing: average last 3–5 forecast values before final output.  
- If true outcome consistently underperforms forecast by >5% over 3–5 periods, apply a downward bias correction of 2–4% per period.  
- If sentiment is rising steadily and forecast is flat, increase forecast by 3–5% to reflect positive momentum.  
- If sentiment is falling and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid overcorrection.
